base/general/off.text: A refrigerator keeps food cold by removing heat energy from the interior and releasing it into the surrounding air. This process relies on a substance called a **refrigerant**, which circulates through coils and undergoes a cycle of evaporation and condensation. As the liquid refrigerant evaporates into a gas, it absorbs heat from the inside of the fridge; this gas is then compressed and moved to outdoor coils, where it releases the heat and condenses back into a liquid. By continuously cycling this heat exchange, the refrigerator lowers the internal temperature, keeping food preserved.
